contexts.text: Be ye prudent as serpents (). Explained. AR 455:end.
Therefore the wife is under the man's prudence.
Had placed the honour of prudence in insidious things.
Ascribe all things to their own prudence. AC 4214:4. AC 6316:end. AC 8478:end. AC 8717:3.
Is insane in proportion as he attributes prudence to himself.
That he applied himself prudently. Signified.
They who attribute all things to their own prudence...
But when anxiety and grief are induced on them... the persuasive is broken... and they can be brought into the faith that... all prudence, etc. are of the Lord.
Civil prudence is believed to be speaking and acting differently from what one thinks and intends...

Simulation and cunning which have good as the end... are prudence; the evils which are admixed with it can be mingled with good... But the simulation and cunning which have evil as the end, are not prudence...
Those under the occiput are those who act silently and prudently.
The five prudent virgins = those who are in truths in which is good.
He who is in good; that is, who acts according to the precepts, is called prudent in... I will liken him to a prudent man ().
From Him without any of their own prudence. Signified, Explained.
The Lord then rules him... by external bonds, which are of Own prudence...
The prudence and circumspection which comes forth in externals, are signified by serpents, in . AC 6949:end.
The evil are permitted to believe that all things are of Own prudence...
Under Provide, see this reference. AC 10779. DP 201:3. DP 210. DP 235.
Those who attribute all things to Own prudence are like those who wander in dense forests.
Prudence avails nothing against fortune. Explained.
Let us use prudence with them () = cunning; (for) prudence, when spoken of by the evil, means cunning; for that which the evil do from cunning and deceit they call prudence.
All who have firmly impressed on themselves that all things are of Own prudence... in the other life are very prone to magic... AC 7296:2. SE 5010.
(Christian prudence to be exercised in works of charity.)
Prudence as to whether he was in safety. Signified.
Simulation, hypocrisy, cunning, and deceit, which are modern prudence...
Not knowing that human prudence is nothing...
Then in place of cunning the Lord implants prudence.

Those who have confirmed themselves for nature and human prudence, do not acknowledge the Divine Providence, because the natural light inflowing from below extinguishes the spiritual light inflowing from above.
From things constant and stated... they find arguments for their delirium in favour of nature and human prudence.
That Own Prudence is null, and only appears to exist, and also ought to appear as if it existed... General article.
Prudence is from God... prudence is from no other source than intelligence and wisdom (and therefore it is only an appearance that it is from man). Explained. DP 193.

Man knows his thoughts and derivative intentions... and as all prudence is from these, he sees it in himself. If, then, his life's love is the love of self, he comes into the pride of Own intelligence, and ascribes prudence to himself; and he collects arguments in its favour, and thus recedes from the acknowledgement of the Divine Providence... In like manner if the love of the world is his life's love; but this does not recede in so great a degree. Thus these two loves ascribe all things to man and his prudence...

Two priests disputing with an ambassador about human prudence... At heart all three believed that human prudence effects all things; but the priests ... said that nothing of prudence is from man. (On changing their garments, they changed also their sentiments.) Afterwards all three entered the way of Own prudence, which tends into Hell. CL 354.
(Arguments showing how little human prudence can do.)
The affections of the life's love are led by the Lord, and the thoughts at the same time, from which is human prudence.

Those who ascribe all things to nature, also ascribe all things to human prudence. Explained. But for the sake of their good name, both say that the Divine Providence is universal, but that its singulars are with man; and that these singulars in the complex are meant by human prudence.
The Divine Providence is in... the most singular things of human prudence...

That those who have acknowledged nature alone and human prudence alone make Hell... Explained. All who lead an evil life, interiorly acknowledge nature and human prudence alone: the acknowledgement of these is inwardly concealed in all evil. DP 205:end. Explained.
Whence and what Own prudence is. It is from man's proprium. Explained.
The mate of the love of self is the pride of Own intelligence; and hence is Own prudence.
The love of self and its mate then sit in the dark and reason... in favour of Own prudence against the Divine Providence.

But those who acknowledge nature and Own prudence are like the Spirits of Hell, who are averse to being led by the Lord, and love to be led by themselves. (Various classes of them described.) They are all enemies of God, and scoffers at the Divine Providence.

Therefore, if you want to be led by the Divine Providence, use prudence, as a servant and minister who faithfully dispenses the goods of his lord. This prudence is the pound which was given to the servants to trade with, an account of which they must render. The prudence itself appears to man as his Own; and is believed to be his Own so long as man keeps within him that most deadly enemy of... the Divine Providence, the love of self... The door for this to be cast out is opened by man's shunning evils as sins as of himself, with the acknowledgement that it is of the Lord. This is the prudence with which the Divine Providence acts as one.

The enmity between thy seed and her seed = that... between the Own prudence of man and the Divine Providence of the Lord; for Own prudence is continually lifting up its head, and the Divine Providence is continually putting it down.
Does not fortune laugh at prudence and wisdom?

But I know that human prudence brings the Rational over to its side more than the Divine Providence does to its; because the latter does not appear, and the former does... But I say to the natural man. Write books, and fill them with arguments... in favour of Own prudence, and an Angel would write on them, They are all appearances and fallacies.
Then originated degrees of dignities... and, with these, the love of self, and the pride of Own prudence.
Those who have confirmed themselves in favour of human prudence... in whatever they see, hear, and read... notice nothing else; nor can they, because they receive nothing from Heaven...
Things of permission... by which the merely natural man confirms himself... in favour of human prudence... Enumerated.
The tree of knowledge = man as to Own prudence.
That victories are on the side of prudence. Explained.
For a good man is in the prudence... of defending; and rarely in any prudence... of invading.
There is not one grain of... Own prudence with any man... If there were, neither Heaven nor Hell would stand, and the whole human race would perish. Explained.
That... Own prudence appropriates both evil and good to men. General article.
What Own prudence is, and what is prudence not man's Own. Explained.

Those are in Own prudence who confirm appearances with themselves, and make them Truths, especially this appearance: that Own prudence is everything, and the Divine Providence not anything, except something universal...
The reason Own prudence persuades and confirms that all good and truth are from man and in man, is that Own prudence is the intellectual proprium of man inflowing from the love of self...

That the simultaneous voluntary and intellectual confirmation of evil causes man to believe Own prudence to be everything, and the Divine Providence not anything; but not intellectual confirmation alone. Explained. There are many who, from the appearances in the world, confirm with themselves Own prudence, but still do not deny the Divine Providence...

That he who confirms with himself the appearance that wisdom and prudence are from man, and in man as his own, cannot see but that otherwise he would not be a man, but either a beast or an image; when yet it is the contrary. Explained.
The proprium of the understanding is the pride of Own intelligence; and from this is Own prudence.
To adore the sun of the world, is to acknowledge... Own prudence as the effectress of all things.
[155a]. The wives said, Be prudent...
The prudence of wives. CL 161:2. CL 166.
The virtues which pertain to the moral wisdom of the men are called prudence, etc.
The innate prudence in virgins.
That these conjugial simulations with natural men savour of prudence...
Infants have no prudence from proprium...
Prudence in military commanders.
That the benefactions of charity are to give to the poor, etc., but with prudence. General article. TCR 428.
These arcana are to be stated prudently.
A sagacious and clearsighted man.
On those who confide in Own prudence... Spirits are permitted to lead, persuade, and induce cupidity on such...

In order that those in faith may not trust in their own prudence, they rarely obtain the things they desire while they desire them; but they obtain them afterwards, if they are useful to them, when they are not thinking about them.
On those who from their success here have contracted the persuasion that they should attribute everything to their own prudence.
I wondered whence came such sagacity, cunning, ...
Whatever man does of his own prudence tends to evil; if not apparently so here, yet visibly so in the other life.
Hence, from light are thought, apperception, reflection, animadvertence, prudence, ...
On the Hell of those who... act with deliberation, circumspection, and prudence.
On... Own prudence and wisdom.
The five prudent virgins = those in love and thence in faith. AE 252:8. AE 375:41. AE 675:6. AE 840:3.
But cunning and malice are not prudence and intelligence...
Serpents = the sensuous man as to cunning, and as to prudence. Illustrated.
Be ye prudent as serpents: Those are called prudent who are in good; cunning, those who are in evil.
This is meant by: The sons of this age are more prudent than the sons of light... ().
He then shuns evils and does goods with prudence, intelligence, and wisdom.
The Lord... permits that man should rather attribute the things which take place to prudence... than that by manifest signs of Providence... he should unseasonably cast himself into sanctities...
The tenth law of the Divine Providence is that man from Own prudence shall lead himself to eminence and opulence when these seduce... Explained.
